gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-001 explicitly identifies that the iteration minimizes the projected-mass quotient with denominator ||P_H v||², whereas the standard LOD problem minimizes the quotient with denominator ||v||², and correctly explains why scalar rescaling cannot convert one minimizer into the other.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both identify the false equivalence between the projected-mass-normalized fixed point and the standard L²-normalized LOD Ritz minimizer: the two Rayleigh quotients generally have different minimizing directions, so scaling does not establish the claimed implication.

component_coverage.gold_component: The claimed scalar-rescaling implication from the projected-mass-constrained minimizer to the standard L²-constrained LOD minimizer is false because the two Rayleigh quotients generally have different minimizing directions.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction states both quotient formulations, explains that ||P_H v||/||v|| is not constant, rejects the rescaling argument, and supplies a repair that separates the projected-mass problem from the standard LOD minimizer.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-003 concerns the unproved extension of a fixed-step convergence theorem to an argmin-selected step sequence and the associated lower/upper step-size range. It does not identify the specific quartic-to-quadratic absorption condition 4τ₀²E(u⁰)<1 required in lemma:Rnorm, nor provide that corrected reciprocal bound.
